text:
devon: FYI Acme Bio wants a focused run-through tomorrow on three things: RBAC change proofs, KMS access evidence, and our vuln-triage containment artifacts. They also want a SIEM-friendly sample and a short story showing chain-of-custody. Can we assemble a tiny demo pack?

maria: yes. can we keep it tight 
(1 slide per topic + a sanitized log bundle). they asked for examples they can ingest into Splunk/Elastic.

kevin: I can produce 3 compact log lines and a mapping doc. recommended export fields: tenant_id, request_id, actor, event, resource, result, ts, key_id, prompt_hash, approval_ticket.

natalie: add policy_id and change_author for RBAC events. We also tag export files with a manifest_sig and manifest_timestamp for signed exports.

kevin: sample RBAC update (sanitized):
```
{"event":"rbac.policy.update","policy_id":"policy-ACME-99","change_author":"maria","diff":"+allow svc:dedicated -> model:invoke","approval_ticket":"INC-12345","ts":"2026-04-01T09:12:00Z"}
```

maria: good. next show an authz check correlating to that change. include prompt_hash so they can map to a prompt without revealing content.

kevin: authz check example:
```
{"event":"authz.check","actor":"svc:dedicated-gw","resource":"model:rdw-gptx-4","result":"allowed","request_id":"req-xyz-1001","prompt_hash":"sha256:deadbeef...","ts":"2026-04-01T09:12:12Z"}
```

natalie: and KMS op snippet, showing denied unwrap (so we can demonstrate nobody unwrapped during the window):
```
{"event":"kms.key_op","key_id":"kms:prod/rdw-key-01","op":"unwrap","caller":"user:ops-admin","status":"denied","ip":"10.5.6.7","ts":"2026-04-01T09:12:13Z"}
```

devon: that covers the happy demo. For auditors theyll want to see retention and redaction rules. What's our published stance?

maria: by default we redact prompt_text in exported logs (prompt_text: REDACTED). We keep a prompt_hash for correlation. Customers can opt-in to richer exports under contract.

kevin: also note: customer SIEM ingest is delivered via encrypted pub/sub push or S3 delivery with envelope signatures. We provide a mapping CSV and an example ingestion event.

natalie: on vuln triage: summarize our containment steps if runtime KV cache suspected: 1) isolate affected nodepool (auto-evacuate), 2) rotate ephemeral serving keys, 3) flip to stateless serve (cache-miss mode), 4) trigger per-tenant exposure scan, 5) generate signed audit export and notify impacted tenants.

devon: auditors will ask for proof we didn't query tenant data during investigation. How do we show that?

natalie: we produce a signed read-only export of the logstore query (hash the query, sign the payload, include manifest_sig). Also snapshot KMS admin events to show no key unwraps.

maria: Acme also requested timeline SLAs for Dedicated: containment within 48h, mitigation plan within 7d, RCA published within 14d. We should state escalation contacts too.

kevin: one more practical item: ensure all timestamps in demo are RFC3339 and tenant identifiers use tenant_redacted.

devon: please assemble:
- 1-page cheat sheet (fields + redaction rules)
- sanitized log bundle (3 example events + manifest)
- one-slide vuln-triage timeline + escalation contacts

maria: I'll draft the cheat sheet and the slide. Kevin, can you build the sanitized bundle and signed manifest example?

kevin: yes. manifest example (placeholder):
```
manifest_sig: "sig:v1:MEQCIH...", manifest_ts: "2026-04-01T09:20:00Z"
bundle_files: ["rbac_update.json","authz_check.json","kms_op.json"]
```

natalie: I'll add the containment checklist and the sample SIEM mapping (CSV) to the bundle.

ir-bot: PREP REMINDER: meeting in 45m. Checklist: [cheatsheet], [sanitized bundle], [SIEM mapping CSV], [runbook link], [contacts]. :calendar:

devon: thanks. quick final ask: include a short note on private HSM vs hosted KMS differences for audits (signed manifests for HSM, richer operator logs for hosted). Keep it one paragraph.

maria: noted. I'll ping for a quick review in 20.

kevin: will post the sanitized bundle to the shared prep channel once it's ready.

devon: perfect. see you on the prep call. :thumbsup:
